newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Ecuador relaunches oil exploration initiative.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador relaunches oil exploration initiative.

text.p: Ecuador is planning three new oil licensing rounds in the near future in a bid to revive the country's flagging upstream industry, Ecuadorean oil officials said on Wednesday.

The biggest project is in the Ishpingo-Tambococha-Tiputini- Imuya (ITTI) heavy crude oilfields in the central-eastern Amazon region. This project alone requires $1 billion in investment and the licensing process should be announced within the next few weeks, an oil ministry spokesman said Wednesday.
Other projects include a marginal fields round, an enhanced recovery tender and a traditional exploration licence round, the ninth of its kind.

The ITTI complex was discovered by PetroEcuador and contains 720 million barrels of proven and probable reserves of heavy 15 API crude, according to a speech given by PetroEcuador president Rafael Almeida to a London conference last month.

"At present, PetroEcuador has the necessary pre-contractual documents to start the international bidding process and approval of the corresponding schedule by the special bidding committee is expected shortly," he told the conference.
He said the exploration period in the contract would last only two years, down from a normal four, because the fields have already been discovered.
"The minimum exploration program mainly contemplates step-out wells to confirm the volume of reserves," he said.
The winner of the tender would also build a new heavy crude pipeline to carry the oil to the coast and this could be done in association with other companies.
Almeida also said ten oilfields were candidates for inclusion in a marginal fields licensing round to be announced in June with the deadline for bids in late September, Almeida added.
He hoped for $140 million investment in these fields to extract 80 million barrels of crude.
Ecuador was also conducting enhanced recovery studies in three of its largest fields, Shushufindi, Sacha and Libertador, that should be completed in the next few months.
Shell said last month it was interested in participating in this project.

A ninth oil exploration licence round was also on the cards, Almeida told the conference, for prospect areas in the Amazon and offshore Pacific coast although the exact blocks have not been decided. Ecuador's existing production-sharing contract would be used, under which all risk capital is provided by the contractor company, he added.
